problems.stem: Your Module 5 capstone deck is due. Which submission shows you carried the whole pipeline, not just polish?
options: A deck with a slick theme and animations but no stated purpose and a failed contrast check.
A deck that names its audience and purpose, uses assertion headlines, has one verified explanatory chart with a source line, narration that adds reasoning, and passes contrast and alt-text checks.
Twelve unedited AI-generated slides submitted as is.
A single resume slide with decorative fonts.
problems.explanation: The strong capstone integrates every Module 5 layer (purpose, structure, media, narration, citation, accessibility) before polish.

problems.stem: Which note gives BigAL a useful capstone-integration problem?
options: My deck has purpose, structure, and citations, but slide 3's narration just rereads the chart and slide 5 fails contrast. Which do I fix first for the panel?
problems.explanation: The note names specific pipeline gaps (narration and contrast) and asks for prioritized feedback for the audience.

problems.stem: What is a defensible role for AI in the capstone?
options: Have AI build and finalize the entire deck for you.
Use AI for bounded moves (draft alt text, critique the headline arc), then make and document every integration decision yourself.
Let AI invent the data and citations so the deck looks complete.
Use AI only to apply a theme and submit.
problems.explanation: AI assists single bounded moves; the capstone must show your own integrated judgment and a revision trail.

problems.stem: Which capstone record best supports a fair review of your work?
options: The before/after of one slide, the issue you noticed, the AI or peer support used, and one suggestion you rejected with the reason.
problems.explanation: A revision trail with a rejected suggestion makes your decisions across the pipeline inspectable.
